replacements.why:
THE CLOSE-OUT REPAIR — 045-10 and 045-41, which is TWO of the six items the close-out pass called one pass.

THE TOOL DECIDED WHICH TWO, AND IT WAS RIGHT. `apply-read-class.py` refuses a replacement that drops a word, because a rewrite which silently deletes prose is this feature's worst failure mode. It fired twice:

  045-7   WORDS DROPPED {'falls': 1}                       a TENSE correction
  045-20  WORDS DROPPED {'rate': 1, 'limiter': 1, ...}     a factual correction to a rationale

**This table is for REFERENCE decisions, and neither a tense nor a rationale is a reference.** 045-10 and 045-41 pass the guard because they move or re-case the SAME words: `CHAPTER's` to `CHAPTER'S`, and a parenthetical re-flowed off the end of its line. That is the line the guard draws, and it draws it better than the estimate did.

045-10 is also larger than its entry says. It reads as five possessives in five tagged chapters; measured across all 26 tags they are five DISTINCT LINES that persist to the tip — the tool fix stopped new ones and never rewrote the existing five.

AND THE EIGHT PAREN PAIRS WERE HAND-TYPED ONCE AND SEVEN OF THEM MISSED. They were built from `sed -n "$ln,$((ln+1))p" | sed 's/^/    /'` — display output — so every one carried four spaces of indentation the file does not have, and only the single unindented case fired. Regenerated FROM THE FILES, where the indentation cannot be wrong: read the line, read its continuation, move the `(` past the continuation's comment marker. **A pair typed from a terminal is a pair typed from a rendering.**
